title: Derived Nakayama from the first reduction
statement:
Let $K\in D(X_{\Proet},\mathcal O_E)$ be derived complete in the sense of
[sk-def-pe-derived-completion]. If $K_1=0$, then $K_n=0$ for all $n\geq1$ and
$K=0$. Derived complete complexes are closed under cones (and shifts), and a
morphism $f\colon K\to L$ of derived complete complexes is an isomorphism as soon
as $f_1=f\otimes^{\mathbf L}(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E)_X\colon K_1\to L_1$ is an
isomorphism.

proof.text: Compare the canonical integral-level reduction with the tensor reduction of det-pe-derived-nakayama-resolution: on a complex representative both are isomorphic to the same scalar cone, by lem-pe-principal-reduction-cone-calculus and the resolution theorem. The scalar endomorphisms agree by evaluation on every profinite section. If K_1 is zero, its restriction is zero. Transport through the comparison and induct on n using the successive coefficient triangle K_1 -> K_(n+1) -> K_n ->. Mathlib Triangle.isZero₂_of_isZero₁₃ gives the induction step.

All integral levels are zero by step 1. The discrete diagram is therefore a zero object in the functor category. Its zero cone is limiting by IsLimit.ofIsZero, giving the required product without a general product-existence theorem. Its chosen limit is zero by IsLimit.isZero_pt. On the K-flat representative supplied by completeness, sk-def-pe-derived-completion gives roos_isDerivedLimit. Both product vertices of that distinguished triangle are zero, so Triangle.isZero₁_of_isZero₂₃ makes the Roos object zero. The specified completion map is invertible by the definition of completeness, hence K is zero. Finally each actual finite-coefficient reduction of K is zero since it is a left adjoint and preserves zero morphisms.

source.place: Vanishing paragraph: zero derived limit and completeness

proof.text: For a distinguished triangle $K\to L\to C\to K[1]$ with $K,L$ complete, [lem-pe-completion-triangle-comparison] gives the distinguished image triangle and the triangle morphism $(c_K,c_L,c_C)$. The first two components are isomorphisms by [sk-def-pe-derived-completion], so [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] makes $c_C$ an isomorphism: $C$ is complete. The same comparison gives $c_{K[r]}=\sigma_{K,r}^{-1}c_K[r]$ for every integer $r$; both factors are isomorphisms when $K$ is complete, so every shift is complete.

source.place: Cones paragraph: two-isomorphism criterion and shifts

proof.text: Complete f to a distinguished triangle T with cone C. Step 3 makes C complete. The first integral reduction has the exact shift structure supplied by lem-pe-principal-reduction-cone-calculus, so its image of T is distinguished. The reduced f is invertible because restriction preserves isomorphisms. The zero-cone criterion gives zero first integral reduction of C. Steps 1-2, already formulated for the integral first reduction, give C=0. The same zero-cone criterion on T then gives IsIso f.

source.place: Isomorphisms paragraph: reduction of the cone
